hero.headline: When a system acts on people, make authority, consequence, contest, and repair visible.
hero.support: A structured audit for consequential software, AI, and institutional processes: who can act, what representation authorizes the action, who bears the consequence, what meaningful options remain, and who owns repair.

sections.heading: Map authority
sections.body: Identify who or what may act, where that authority came from, what it permits, and where delegation or automation changes the chain.

sections.heading: Inspect representation
sections.body: Determine which categories, data, models, records, and interfaces stand in for the affected person or condition.

sections.heading: Trace consequence
sections.body: Follow a decision beyond its immediate output into access, eligibility, status, workload, recourse, cost, risk, and downstream institutional behavior.

sections.heading: Test contestability
sections.body: Ask whether an affected party can understand, challenge, suspend, correct, or reverse the process in practice rather than merely in policy.

sections.heading: Assign repair
sections.body: A consequential system is incomplete when it can impose effects but cannot identify who must correct the representation and repair the resulting harm or error.

pilot.shape: Audit one bounded process involving eligibility, identity, access, moderation, benefits, automated management, or another consequential classification.
